analysis: The trial executed successfully but reduced host validation macro HR@10 from the supplied reference 0.6275 to 0.6013, a decline of 0.0262. Category HR@10 was Movies_and_TV 0.650, Industrial_and_Scientific 0.640, Electronics 0.415, and CDs_and_Vinyl 0.700. Electronics remained weakest and fell from the supplied reference of 0.425. The direct latest-item residual hypothesis was not supported by this run. Zero initialization preserves initial encoder behavior but does not prevent the learned residual from worsening validation ranking. These results do not establish the cause of the decline. Allocated GPU time was 1155.99 seconds; no test results were available.
code_summary: One independently trained LightGCN per category, with 64-dimensional embeddings, three propagation layers, tied item vectors, learned item bias, and gated attention over up to 128 history events. Attention keys include relative positions; queries combine the propagated user vector and a learned latest-item projection. This experiment added a zero-initialized linear projection of the latest propagated item directly to the fused user/history representation, including singleton histories; empty histories retain the user vector. Training retains prefix supervision, minibatch supervised-edge removal with graph renormalization, sampled-negative cross-entropy, embedding regularization, and Adam. Diagnostics check initialization parity, gathering, gradients, scoring, and serialization. The predictor strictly restores one selected checkpoint per category and shares history encoding across known and unknown users. No ensembles or separately fitted scorers are used.
